tier_reason: The wiki pages time libc memcpy/memset ('standard memcpy', 'standard memset') and the project's own C, NEON, ARM and SSE2 kernels in the same run, and every number in the record matches the raw wiki markdown; but the harness is the project's own program (main.c, asm-opt.c, arm-neon.S, x86-sse2.S) and no page records compiler, flags or libc version, so it is not A, and a first-party harness run by community contributors (the BeagleBone Black page was added by a third-party account on 2017-03-21) is not an independent suite, so C rather than B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No headline claim; results are per-board wiki tables (ratios derived from page data). BeagleBone Black (Cortex-A8 AM3358 r2.1 at 1 GHz, tinymembench v0.4.9): standard memcpy 258.3 MB/s vs 'C copy prefetched (32 bytes step)' 505.1 MB/s (1.96x), 'ARM copy prefetched (wrap pld)' 508.4 MB/s (1.97x) and 'NEON copy prefetched (32 bytes step)' 563.5 MB/s (2.18x); standard memset 1511.9 MB/s is level with every custom fill (1510.6 to 1512.0 MB/s). Allwinner A13 (v0.2.9): standard memcpy 249.8 vs 'C copy prefetched (32 bytes step)' 406.5 MB/s (1.63x) and 'NEON unrolled copy' 499.9 MB/s (2.00x). Intel Core i7-8700T (v0.4.9): standard memcpy 16647.8 vs 'SSE2 nontemporal copy' 17273.1 MB/s (1.04x); standard memset 32815.6 vs 'SSE2 nontemporal fill' 41097.4 MB/s (1.25x). Raspberry Pi BCM2835 at stock 700 MHz with Raspbian 2015-01-31: libc memcpy 387.6 MB/s is level with the best custom copy (392.6 MB/s) and libc memset 1458.5 MB/s ties 'ARM fill (STM with 4 registers)' 1458.4 MB/s; on the same page's overclocked run with a custom 4.1.15 kernel, standard memcpy 307.9 vs 'C copy prefetched' 543.5 MB/s (1.77x). AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D: standard memcpy 81381.2 vs best custom 'SSE2 copy prefetched (64 bytes step)' 81804.8 MB/s (1.005x, a tie), standard memset 156460.7 vs 'SSE2 fill' 162148.8 MB/s (1.04x), and the SSE2 nontemporal copy (32028.6 MB/s) is 2.5x slower than libc.
corrections.caveats: The harness is the project's own benchmark program, and the wiki pages (68 pages, community-submitted; the BeagleBone Black page came from a third-party contributor in March 2017) record neither compiler, flags nor libc version, so the baseline is whatever libc memcpy each OS image shipped. The ARM wins come from 2012 to 2017 era boards (Cortex-A8, Allwinner A13) whose glibc memcpy lacked prefetching or NEON loops; they may not hold for current glibc, Bionic or Arm optimized-routines, and stock Raspbian (which preloads its own copy routines) already matches the best kernel. On modern x86 libc memcpy ties or beats every custom copy (Ryzen 9800X3D 81381.2 vs 81804.8 MB/s; nontemporal copies 2.5x slower there), and the only x86 wins are 4 to 25 percent from nontemporal stores on an i7-8700T. Libc memset is level with the custom fills on BeagleBone Black and Raspberry Pi. Runs span tinymembench v0.2.9 to v0.4.9 and many contributors. Results are large-block bandwidth with aligned buffers, not small-copy latency or correctness-checked memcpy replacements: the kernels are benchmark loops inside a test program (MIT), not a packaged memcpy library. The code repository has had no commit since 2017-02-14, though the wiki still receives runs (Ryzen 9800X3D, Core i9-13900K pages).

notes: Numbers verified line by line against the raw wiki markdown (BeagleBone Black, Allwinner A13, i7-8700T, Raspberry Pi BCM2835, Ryzen 9800X3D); downgraded B to C because the harness is first-party and no compiler, flags or libc versions are recorded. Shortcomings: no compiler/flags/libc version on any page; wins only against 2012-2017 ARM libcs; libc memcpy ties or beats every custom copy on modern x86 and stock Raspbian; benchmark kernels rather than a drop-in library; code abandoned since 2017. Metadata (MIT, 418 stars, 102 forks, last commit 2017-02-14, not a fork) confirmed.

tier_reason: README-PERFORMANCE.md states the asm-versus-compiler gains only in prose ('up 60% with MULX, ADCX, ADOX on BLS12-381 (6 limbs)', '~60% faster than Clang', '2.4x perf ratio between using plain GCC vs GCC with inline assembly', 'GCC is up to 2x slower than Clang'); the benchmark tasks are public but no table, CPU, compiler version or run log backs these figures, and the published charts (Ryzen 7 7840U, i9-9980XE) show Constantine-only absolute timings with no assembly-off column, so first-party numbers without methodology: C.

corrections.hardware: No CPU named for the asm-versus-compiler statements; the charts in README-PERFORMANCE.md are Constantine-only runs on an AMD Ryzen 7 7840U (Zen 4; EVM precompiles, KZG, BLS signatures, BLS12-381 summary and MSM) and an i9-9980XE (BN254 MSM), none with an assembly-off comparison
corrections.caveats: The asm-versus-compiler percentages are prose statements with no table, CPU, compiler version or run log for the 60% and 2.4x figures, and the same file's compiler figures disagree with each other (GCC 'up to 2x slower than Clang', '~50% slower than Clang', and Clang/MSVC/ICC 'up to 20~25% faster than GCC'). The 2.4x is plain GCC versus GCC with inline assembly, roughly the product of GCC's carry-handling penalty and the MULX/ADCX/ADOX gain, so against a Clang build the asm gain is the stated ~60%. The published benchmark charts (Ryzen 7 7840U, i9-9980XE) show only Constantine's own absolute timings (for example Fp[BLS12_381] multiplication 20 ns / 68 cycles), with no CTT_ASM=0 column and no comparison against blst, mcl, gnark-crypto or other libraries. Assembly is x86-64 only; ARM builds use the compiler path.

notes: Quotes match README-PERFORMANCE.md verbatim; C stands as first-party prose numbers without methodology. Shortcomings: no table, CPU or run log behind the 60%/2.4x claims; internally inconsistent GCC-versus-Clang figures; charts carry no asm-off or external-library comparison; asm only on x86-64.
